headline: Community Lighthouses: When Neighbors Power Each Other Through Crisis
meta_description: Churches and community centers in Louisiana are installing solar panels to provide emergency electricity when hurricanes strike, creating resilient neighborhoo…

body:
When Hurricane Francine knocked out power across New Orleans in 2024, Pastor Shawn Anglim unlocked First Grace United Methodist Church and switched on the lights. Within hours, more than 100 people had gathered inside—charging medical devices, cooling off in air conditioning, and finding refuge from the heat. Anglim's church is one of 14 Community Lighthouses now operating in New Orleans, each equipped with solar panels and battery systems designed to provide electricity when the grid fails. The concept emerged from necessity: Hurricane Ida in 2021 left parts of the city without power for 12 days, triggering a deadly heatwave and prompting local leaders to ask what they could do differently.

The idea took shape during a Zoom conversation among faith and community leaders. After securing $1 million from the Greater New Orleans Foundation, Together New Orleans launched the project in 2022. What began as what Anglim calls "the most far-fetched idea" has now expanded beyond emergency response. The Lighthouses feed excess power back into the grid during normal operations, strengthening the city's energy resilience. More importantly, they become natural gathering points where other services converge—food banks, oxygen supplies, and portable generators all found their way to Anglim's church during Francine's aftermath because power was available there.

Success requires careful planning. Volunteer "lighthouse keepers" coordinate teams, ensuring someone is present to open doors, distribute supplies, and monitor battery systems when disaster strikes. Though people may need to work or evacuate, Anglim has found that other volunteers naturally step in to fill gaps. The model is spreading: Houston has already secured funding for its first Community Lighthouse, and interest is growing across the United States. For Anglim, the real message is simpler: "We need to have skin in the game. This is our community too."
quick_facts: 14 Community Lighthouses now operating in New Orleans with solar panels
Hurricane Francine 2024: 100+ people sheltered at First Grace Methodist Church
Initial funding: $1 million from Greater New Orleans Foundation in 2022
Louisiana experiences most power interruptions and longest blackouts in U.S.
